findings.key_quote: In Q1 2026, a portion of the then-outstanding notes was converted to nonvoting preferred stock... a gain of approximately $ 3.3 billion and $ 4.5 billion was recorded in "Other income (expense), net." In Q1 2026, we also recorded an upward adjustment of approximately $ 12.3 billion to our nonvoting preferred stock in "Other income (expense), net" to reflect observable changes in price.
findings.justification: This evidence shows that Q1 2026 included one-time gains totaling approximately $16.8 billion ($4.5 billion from conversion + $12.3 billion from upward adjustment) related to Anthropic investments recorded in Other income (expense), net. These are non-operating gains that would flow through to operating income if they affected the operating income calculation, but more importantly, these are one-time items from investment valuations that overstate underlying profitability.

findings.key_quote: The reclassification adjustments for the gains on available-for-sale debt securities of $ 3.3 billion and $ 4.5 billion in Q1 2025 and Q1 2026 are primarily from the portions of our convertible notes investments in Anthropic, PBC ("Anthropic") that were converted to nonvoting preferred stock during Q1 2025 and Q1 2026. The upward adjustments relating to equity investments in private companies of $ 12.3 billion in Q1 2026 reflect observable changes in prices, primarily from our nonvoting preferred stock in Anthropic.
findings.justification: This evidence confirms that Q1 2026 included $4.5 billion in reclassification gains and $12.3 billion in upward adjustments (totaling $16.8 billion) from Anthropic investments. These are one-time gains from investment valuations that are not part of recurring operations and would overstate underlying profitability.

findings.key_quote: Our income tax provision for the three months ended March 31, 2026 was $ 9.6 billion, which included $ 4.1 billion of net discrete tax expense primarily attributable to the net gains from our investments in Anthropic.
findings.justification: This evidence shows that Q1 2026 included $4.1 billion of discrete tax expense related to the Anthropic investment gains. This is a one-time tax item directly tied to the one-time investment gains, further supporting that one-time items affected the quarter's results. While this is a tax expense (not income), it's a one-time item that affects net income and is tied to the one-time gains.

findings.key_quote: Operating income increased from $18.4 billion in Q1 2025 to $23.9 billion in Q1 2026.
findings.justification: This provides the level of operating income for Q1 2026 but does not address whether one-time items benefited operating income or whether they overstate underlying profitability. The claim is about operating income being affected by one-time items, but this passage only reports the operating income level without discussing one-time items' impact on it.

findings.key_quote: Other income (expense), net was $2.7 billion and $15.6 billion during Q1 2025 and Q1 2026. The net gain of $2.7 billion in Q1 2025 is primarily from the reclassification adjustment for the gain on available-for-sale debt securities from the portion of our convertible notes investments in Anthropic that were converted to nonvoting preferred stock during Q1 2025.
findings.justification: This shows that Other income (expense), net was $15.6 billion in Q1 2026, which is below the operating income line on the income statement. While this contains the one-time Anthropic gains, it does not directly address whether operating income itself benefited from one-time items. The claim specifically references operating income, not other income.

findings.key_quote: Other operating expense (income), net was $308 million and $447 million for Q1 2025 and Q1 2026, and was primarily related to charges associated with damaged data centers in the Middle East in Q1 2026, asset impairments, and the amortization of intangible assets.
findings.justification: This mentions charges for damaged data centers in Q1 2026, which could be considered a one-time item, but these are expenses (not income) that would reduce operating income rather than overstate profitability. The claim is about items that overstate profitability, so this is related but does not decide the assertion.

findings.key_quote: Our income tax provision for the three months ended March 31, 2026 was $ 9.6 billion, which included $ 4.1 billion of net discrete tax expense primarily attributable to the net gains from our investments in Anthropic.
findings.justification: This provides context on the tax impact of the Anthropic gains but is about income tax provision, which is below operating income on the income statement. It does not directly address whether operating income benefited from one-time items.
